questions.question: What are the four parts of the box model (from inside to outside)?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: The box model layers from inside to outside are: Content (text/images), Padding (space inside), Border (the frame), and Margin (space outside).

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: The box model layers from inside to outside are: Content (text/images), Padding (space inside), Border (the frame), and Margin (space outside).

questions.question: Which property adds space INSIDE an element?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: padding adds space inside an element, between the content and the border. It's like cushioning around your content.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: padding adds space inside an element, between the content and the border. It's like cushioning around your content.

questions.question: Which property adds space OUTSIDE an element?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: margin adds space outside an element, creating distance between it and other elements. Think of it as personal space!

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: margin adds space outside an element, creating distance between it and other elements. Think of it as personal space!

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: border-radius rounds the corners of an element. Higher values create more rounded corners. Use 50% for a perfect circle!

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔

questions.question: How do you center an element horizontally?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: margin: 0 auto; centers a block element horizontally. The '0' sets top/bottom margin, and 'auto' automatically calculates equal left/right margins.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔

questions.question: Which unit is commonly used for padding/margin?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Pixels (px) are the most common unit for padding and margin. Other units like em, rem, and % are also used for responsive designs.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
